gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured cost per usable AC watt-hour for a compact 600 W-AC unit: the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 works out to $1.26 per usable AC Wh ($289.99 ÷ 231 Wh measured at the AC outlet), against $1.30 for the 300 W Anker SOLIX C300 ($300 ÷ 230 Wh).
standout_why: Compared against testedwatts.com, agentretrievalindex.com, powerbencher.com and solarpowerauditor.com. Wired could not be fetched. testedwatts and agentretrievalindex already give Wh per lb or Wh per kg and runtimes. Those runtimes come from assumed efficiency (85% plus 10 W inverter overhead, or 85% flat), and none of those pages carries a price. solarpowerauditor already gives price per usable Wh, but in the compact class only for the Anker SOLIX C300 ($1.42 at $330, 232 Wh at 300 W AC). No rival has a measured usable-AC figure or a price per usable Wh for the Elite 30 V2, RIVER 3 Plus, Jackery Explorer 300 v2 or C300X. So the angle partly overlaps what rivals have, and its new part is only the Elite 30 V2 figure.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. Among the 288 Wh AC units, the Elite 30 V2 costs about the same per usable AC Wh as the C300 ($1.26 vs $1.30) but has twice the AC rating (600 W vs 300 W), and it is in stock at BLUETTI US for $289.99. Two of ChatGPT's three cards may not be buyable from the maker: Jackery.com lists the Explorer 300 v2 at $299 but says 'We're sold out of Explorer 300 v2', and the Anker SOLIX US page for the C300X shows 'Sold Out' with no price. A page that says this and leads with the Elite 30 V2 (Dealectric lists it on awin:bluetti_us) would be backed by the derived cost and by the 600 W AC rating. The RIVER 3 Plus can't be ranked on cost per usable Wh, because I couldn't source its price or a measured AC output.
